title: Where Earth's water is
subtitle: Almost all of it is salty, and most fresh water is frozen.

items.label: Oceans
items.detail: Salt water covers about 71% of the surface and holds nearly all of Earth's water.

items.label: Ice caps and glaciers
items.detail: Most fresh water is locked in Antarctica and Greenland.

items.label: Groundwater
items.detail: Stored in rock and soil; about half of it is salty.

items.label: Lakes and rivers
items.detail: All the surface fresh water we see is a tiny sliver of the total.

title: How a vaccine trains your body

items.label: Harmless piece arrives
items.detail: The vaccine carries a weakened germ or a piece of one, such as a spike protein, that can't make you sick.

items.label: Immune system notices
items.detail: White blood cells spot the unfamiliar piece and raise the alarm.

items.label: Antibodies are made
items.detail: B cells build antibodies shaped to lock onto that exact piece.

items.label: Memory stays
items.detail: Memory cells remember it for years, so a real infection is stopped fast.

items.label: Joins across tables
items.detail: Relations are first-class: one query can combine customers, orders and products.

items.label: Scales out easily
items.detail: Data is spread across many machines, so adding servers adds capacity.
